what_it_does: This paper addresses distributed quantum computing systems where multiple quantum processors need to create entangled (linked) quantum states across a network. The core challenge is that creating these entangled pairs is probabilistic (unreliable) and slow, so naive approaches waste time waiting for successful entanglement. The paper proposes storing successfully-created entangled pairs in a buffer, continuously attempting to generate new pairs in parallel while the quantum processor runs gate operations (instructions), and adapting which operations to run based on what entangled pairs are available.
